speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior; can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD).

The rapid onset of cerebellar signs (weakness, ataxia, falls) combined with rapidly progressive dementia and behavioral changes over just 6-7 months is highly characteristic of CJD. I am requesting results for a CSF analysis for 14-3-3 protein and RT-PCR, along with an MRI of the brain to look for cortical ribboning.
